summary: NASA has announced plans to accelerate its Artemis program to return to the Moon, alongside revealing the new X-70 experimental aircraft to advance aeronautics research. Following the 2026 midterm elections, a presidential proclamation asserted American space superiority, while the U.S. Space Force Chief eyed growth in force components to meet operational demands. In commercial space, Redwire secured a $20 million DARPA contract for a second Very Low Earth Orbit demonstration, NASA awarded contracts for Ka-Band satellite relay communications, and Orbital Matter partnered with EnduroSat for a planned 2028 in-space manufacturing mission; conversely, Starfish Space lost contact with its Otter vehicle, prematurely ending the SSPICY mission. Scientific developments include European orbiter data revealing fresh evidence of recent volcanic activity on Mars, promising preliminary results from a NASA planetary landing navigation experiment, and the discovery of a giant planet within James Webb Space Telescope data using a glare-removal technique. Additionally, NASA's Swift space telescope re-entered Earth's atmosphere after two decades of operation following an unsuccessful rescue effort. Readers should watch for two astronauts completing upgrades to the International Space Station's solar arrays during a live-streamed spacewalk scheduled for today.
